question: HVAC unit consuming 25% more power than normal. Fan speed unchanged. What is the cause?
resolution:
Root cause: Dirty evaporator coil increasing system resistance. The power draw rises while airflow drops.
Immediate action: Reduce set-point by 2°C to prevent compressor short-cycling.
Permanent fix: 1) Shut down AHU. 2) Remove access panel. 3) Apply coil cleaner (part: COIL-CLN-5L) and rinse. 4) Replace air filter (part: FILTER-G4-600x600). 5) Restart and verify power normalises within 30 minutes.
Parts: COIL-CLN-5L (coil cleaner), FILTER-G4-600x600 (G4 filter)
Estimated time: 2.5 hours

question: AHU bearing noise and vibration increasing over 2 weeks. Motor current slightly elevated.
resolution:
Root cause: Progressive bearing wear in supply fan motor. Vibration increase of >1.5mm/s from baseline indicates imminent failure.
Immediate action: Reduce fan speed to 70% via BMS override to extend bearing life.
Permanent fix: 1) Schedule planned outage. 2) Isolate and lock out AHU. 3) Replace supply fan motor bearings (part: BRG-6206-2RS). 4) Rebalance fan assembly. 5) Re-lubricate with Mobil Polyrex EM grease.
Parts: BRG-6206-2RS (deep groove ball bearing x2)
ts: Mobil Polyrex EM (grease cartridge)\nEstimated time: 4 hours

question: Energy meter showing power factor below 0.85. Reactive power spiking at peak hours.
resolution: Root cause: Inductive load increase (likely additional HVAC compressors or UPS units) without corresponding power factor correction capacitor adjustment.\nImmediate action: Check if any new loads were recently connected to this distribution board.\nPermanent fix: 1) Audit all loads on this phase. 2) Adjust PFC capacitor bank steps via panel display (menu: PFC > Auto > Bank 3). 3) Target PF > 0.95. 4) If capacitor bank is at max
ts: install additional 50kVAR stage (part: CAP-50KVAR-415V).\nParts: CAP-50KVAR-415V (power factor capacitor bank) if required\nEstimated time: 1.5 hours

question: Core switch showing 15% error rate on uplink port. Connected devices losing connectivity intermittently.
resolution: Root cause: Physical layer fault on SFP+ uplink — likely dirty fibre connector or degraded SFP transceiver.\nImmediate action: Log into switch CLI and run: show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/49 counters errors. Check CRC errors vs input errors ratio.\nPermanent fix: 1) Clean fibre connectors with IEC 61300-3-35 compliant cleaner. 2) If errors persist
ts: swap SFP transceiver (part: SFP-10G-SR). 3) Re-test with OWL Optical Power Meter to verify signal level > -9 dBm.\nParts: SFP-10G-SR (10G short-range SFP transceiver)

question: Server CPU temperature reaching 78°C. Fan speed at maximum. Ambient room temp is 22°C.
resolution:
Root cause: Clogged server air intake or failed CPU heatsink contact. 78°C is within Intel thermal spec (Tjmax 100°C) but the margin is narrowing.
Immediate action: Check server front panel for blocked intake vents. Clean with compressed air if accessible without shutdown.
Permanent fix: 1) Schedule maintenance window. 2) Shut down and remove server from rack. 3) Clean all fans and heatsinks with compressed air. 4) Replace thermal paste on CPU (part: TX-4 thermal compound). 5) Re-seat heatsink with 4.5Nm torque per Intel spec.
Parts: TX-4 (thermal compound syringe)
Estimated time: 1.5 hours

question: BTS base station showing packet loss >2% on backhaul link. Throughput dropped by 40%.
resolution:
Root cause: Microwave backhaul link degradation — typically caused by antenna misalignment after wind loading or rain fade on unlicensed frequency.
Immediate action: Check RSL (Received Signal Level) in BTS web GUI (Operations > Backhaul > RSL). Normal range: -60 to -75 dBm.
Permanent fix: 1) If RSL is low: schedule antenna realignment with spectrum analyser. 2) If RSL is normal: check Ethernet handoff from ODU — replace ODU-IDU cable if degraded. 3) Verify QoS configuration — prioritise RRC signalling traffic.
Parts: CAT6A-SHIELDED-50M (ODU-IDU cable
ts: if required)\nEstimated time: 3 hours (antenna realignment requires 2-person team with lift)
